content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in early cycles and underperform during sharp downturns.", "Sentiment spikes correlate with price reversals, especially when negative sentiment precedes sharp declines.", "Model forecasts show persistent bias toward higher prices, suggesting underweighting of downward momentum.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment aligns with recent price trends, indicating sentiment-driven calibration is critical.", "Models exhibit lag in reacting to sentiment shifts, particularly when sentiment turns negative mid-cycle.", "Price mean-reversion is stronger in later cycles, suggesting forecasts should adjust downward as volatility declines.", "Forecast overshoots are most pronounced in early 30-day windows, indicating overconfidence in upward momentum.", "Sentiment history should be weighted more heavily in forecasting when price volatility exceeds historical norms."]}
